commitResults.messageBody: Move Edith's banners, dividers, error messages, task list rendering, and task mutation confirmations into a dedicated Ui class. This keeps the command loop responsible for orchestration while preserving existing console output. Refresh the captured Java 25 UI test transcript after all planned sessions pass.

Encapsulate Edith's mutable task collection behind TaskList operations for adding, accessing, removing, sizing, and checking emptiness. Construct it from loaded tasks and provide a read-only snapshot to the existing Storage API, preserving persistence and all console behavior while reducing direct List manipulation in Edith.

Move command recognition, todo/deadline/event construction, date validation, and task-number parsing from Edith into Parser. Edith now coordinates parsed commands with TaskList, Storage, and Ui while retaining the existing validation messages and command behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce command hierarchy for list and exit
commitResults.messageBody: Add an abstract Command contract and migrate the argument-free list and bye behaviors into ListCommand and ExitCommand. Teach Parser to construct these command objects while Edith temporarily retains its switch for commands that still require migration. This establishes polymorphic execution in a small, behavior-preserving step before moving task-mutating commands.

Move mark, unmark, and delete behavior from Edith into dedicated Command subclasses that carry their parsed task numbers, validate list bounds, perform mutations, persist changes, and display confirmations. Extend Parser's incremental command factory for these types and add an exact UI test covering unmark behavior on restored data.

Represent todo, deadline, and event additions with a shared AddCommand that owns insertion, persistence, and confirmation behavior. Consolidate Parser into one parse method that validates input and returns a Command for every supported command type. Remove Edith's remaining command switch and add helper so its loop now only parses, executes, handles errors, and exits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move application lifecycle into Edith run method
commitResults.messageBody: Give Edith ownership of its Ui and TaskList collaborators, move Scanner-based command reading behind Ui, and introduce a run method with a parse-execute-exit loop. Use a finally block for consistent divider output and reduce main to constructing and running the application while preserving EOF and console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for grouped UI output
commitResults.messageBody:
Several UI methods send ordered groups of lines by repeating the same
output call.

Introduce a private varargs helper to express these messages as line
groups while preserving their existing output and order. Record the
successful UI regression test run.

Integrate the grouped UI output refactor after its JUnit and
console UI regression suites pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Centralize parser usage text and markers
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event syntax is repeated across parser error paths. This
invites inconsistent guidance when a command format changes.

Keep each usage string and marker in one named place so parsing and
corrective messages remain easy to read and update together.

Storage decodes deadline and event dates using offsets that give no
clue which saved-file delimiters they skip. Those offsets can drift
if the format changes.

Name the delimiters and derive the offsets from their lengths to
make each field boundary clear while preserving the file format.

Command lookup scans enum values for the first matching keyword. Use a stream filter and findFirst to express that search directly while preserving exact matches, argument rules, and the null result for unknown input.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document task command invariants with assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
Task commands mutate the list and completion state after validating user
input. Their expected results are implicit, making regressions harder to
spot during development.

Assert the list changes and displayed completion state after each
command. Run the planned console tests with assertions enabled and
record their output to verify the existing behavior.
Document task command invariants with assertions
Improve code quality
Include streams where applicable

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tags to newly created tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks need to carry tags before later commands can manage or search
them. Accept optional /tags in all creation commands and display tags
after each task's description and date details.

Store metadata beside existing task lines so legacy files still load
without treating tag-like description text as tags. Cover parsing,
formatting, storage, and console persistence with tests.

Tasks with saved tags need a way to change them after creation. Add
commands that validate every requested tag before changing the
full-list task and report requests that make no change without saving.

Document the syntax and verify case-insensitive tags, numbering,
partial removals, errors, and persistence in JUnit and console tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find tasks by exact tag or matching text
commitResults.messageBody:
Task search only checks descriptions, so saved tags cannot help users
locate tasks. Match an entire valid #tag query against tag names exactly
and case-insensitively. Keep other searches as substring matches across
descriptions and individual tags, preserving task order and numbering.

Document the search rules and add JUnit and console UI coverage for
exact tags, plain text, missing tags, and hashtag phrases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix Checkstyle formatting in tag tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command and parser tests wrap lambda parentheses onto new lines,
which violates the configured SeparatorWrap rule. Keep the lambda
parentheses with their calls and wrap the remaining expression instead.

This changes test formatting only. Checkstyle, the full JUnit suite, and
the planned console UI sessions pass.

Added support for optional tagging during task creation, tagging to existing tasks, and untagging. Also extended find command to match both task description and tag description. Extended find functionality to include searching only by #tag. Ensured original behaviour of adding, deleting, marking, unmarking, and saving remains generally unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add profile photos to chat messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Chat messages use letter badges for their speakers, which makes the
conversation less personal and harder to scan. Use the supplied user
and Edith photos as circular avatars beside their respective messages.

Bundle the images as application resources so they remain available
when the GUI is packaged and launched elsewhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain available commands in GUI welcome
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI greeting gives no guidance on which commands users can enter.
Show the supported task, search, update, tag, and exit commands
in a grouped list so users can start using Edith from the first message.

Bring the chat profile photos and command guide into the main branch.
The merge commit preserves the GUI work as a distinct branch of history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid commands and saved task errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Reject invalid dates, repeated command markers, and duplicate tasks so
users receive corrective errors instead of inconsistent task data.

Validate saved records before use and avoid overwriting a file that
cannot be loaded. Save through a temporary file to protect existing
data when a write fails. Extend JUnit and console UI coverage for these
cases.

Bring validated command parsing, safer task persistence, and
expanded regression coverage into master.
